summary: 'Gynaecological Products' is a therapeutic-category/group descriptor rather than a single medicine. It corresponds to the broad WHO ATC group G ('Genito-urinary system and sex hormones') / gynaecological anti-infectives and agents, and includes a wide range of products used for conditions of the female genital tract: vaginal anti-infectives and antiseptics (e.g. clotrimazole, metronidazole, nystatin, povidone-iodine pessaries), topical/vaginal hormones (e.g. oestrogen creams/pessaries for atrophic vaginitis), vaginal lubricants and moisturisers, intrauterine and contraceptive products, and uterine-acting/labour agents (e.g. oxytocics, prostaglandins). Because the indication, dose, route, contraindications and safety profile depend entirely on the individual product, no single set of dosing or safety statements applies. Clinicians must identify and use the monograph for the specific gynaecological medicine concerned.
indications: Vaginal and lower genital-tract infections (candidiasis, bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis) - via specific anti-infectives
Atrophic vaginitis/genitourinary syndrome of menopause - via topical/vaginal oestrogens
Cervical ripening, labour induction and uterine atony - via specific uterotonics (product-specific)
Other gynaecological indications depending on the individual product

moa: No single mechanism applies. Members of this category act by diverse mechanisms depending on the agent: antifungals (e.g. azoles disrupting fungal ergosterol synthesis), antibacterials/antiprotozoals (e.g. metronidazole), antiseptics (e.g. povidone-iodine), oestrogens acting on vaginal epithelium via oestrogen receptors, lubricants providing physical moisture, and uterotonics (oxytocin/prostaglandins) acting on uterine smooth muscle. The relevant mechanism must be taken from the specific product's monograph.

absolute: Determined by the specific product (e.g. known hypersensitivity to that agent)
relative: Pregnancy/lactation suitability varies entirely by product
monitor: As specified for the individual medicine and indication

preg: Suitability in pregnancy varies completely by product: some vaginal anti-infectives are used in pregnancy, certain agents are contraindicated, and some uterotonics are specifically used only in labour/delivery. Always check the specific product's pregnancy information.
lact: Compatibility with breastfeeding depends on the individual agent and route; many topical/vaginal products have minimal systemic absorption, but the specific product label should be consulted.
renal: Dose adjustment in renal impairment depends entirely on the specific medicine chosen.
hepatic: Dose adjustment in hepatic impairment depends entirely on the specific medicine chosen.

major: Interactions are product-specific (e.g. metronidazole-containing products interact with alcohol and warfarin)
moderate: Depend on the specific agent and its systemic absorption
interactions.alcohol: Product-specific (notably avoid alcohol with metronidazole-type agents)

common: For vaginal preparations: local irritation, itching or discharge are typical (agent-dependent)
emergency: Severe allergic reaction to the specific product - discontinue and seek care

missed: Depends on the specific medicine - for vaginal courses, generally insert the missed dose when remembered and continue; do not double up. Follow the individual product's instructions.
overdose: Overdose management is product-specific. For most vaginal/topical preparations, accidental excess use causes only local irritation; systemic agents in this category are managed per their own labels. Seek advice with the specific product name to hand.
